relevance_note: Family study of Fish Eye disease with an LCAT codon deletion: "the proband and one of his sisters are homozygous for the leu300 deletion"; children and mother heterozygous.
method_note: Built by a short Python script from my own reading; table spans were sliced programmatically from the Table I/II rows and checked. Labels are the Table I/II column headers (patients as columns: 'Proband a', 'Offspring b', 'Offspring c', 'Offspring d', 'Sister e', 'Mother f', 'Uncle g'; the same letters a-g are used in the Fig. 3 legend). Uncle g is a tested relative without the variant ('his paternal uncle is not affected'; same MlnI pattern as control), so he has an individuals row but no variant row. The variant is printed only as a protein-level description ('leu300 deletion', 'LCAT300-del.', 'deletion of an entire codon (CTC) in exon 6'); no HGVS c./p. string or transcript is printed, so cdna/protein HGVS fields are null. Variant type 'in-frame indel' is taken from 'deletion of an entire codon (CTC)'; the paper does not use the word 'in-frame'. Offspring inheritance recorded 'inherited paternal' because their father (the proband) is stated homozygous; proband 'inherited maternal' because his mother is stated heterozygous (one allele; father not tested). Sister: inheritance and consanguinity left 'not reported' because the paper does not state that Mother f is also her mother or that the first-cousin parents are hers. Small inconsistency: Methods say corneal clouding 'before the age of 20', Discussion says corneal opacities 'at age 20'; age at onset recorded from the Discussion. Methods say deteriorating vision 'after the age of 40', Discussion says visual impairment 'by age 40'. The Discussion also says pCER was '27–42% of normal' in the two homozygotes, while Results/Table II say proband pCER 25 vs 59 (≈42%) and the text says 'reduced to 15 and 27%'; recorded the per-person sentence. Triglycerides 'markedly increased ... in three of the four analyzed heterozygotes' is an unnamed count, so no heterozygote gets hypertriglyceridemia; Table I numeric values for heterozygotes were not interpreted as abnormal/normal. 'HDL cholesterol of the heterozygous family members was in the low-normal range' was used (named group, D-27) to exclude low HDL in Offspring b-d and Mother f. The Discussion statement that residual activity in 'the two homozygotes' is 'sufficient to protect from renal disease and anemia' was not used to exclude renal disease or anemia for Sister e (interpretive, not an examination finding). Previously reported FED patients (n = 6/5 mean columns, refs 6, 11, 13) are group means only and get no rows.
